decisions.detail: QUOTE: the default expansion is `private_##member`, so `ctx->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(alg)` becomes `ctx->private_alg` | WHY: The answer states the default rename to `private_<member>`. decisions.mark: explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones

decisions.mark: concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member)` is a rename, not access control... Outside code that writes `ctx->alg` gets a compile error. decisions.mark: identifies that some example programs ALSO define the opt-out for themselves, deliberately reaching past the public API they otherwise demonstrate
